title: ReNO: Enhancing One-step Text-to-Image Models through Reward-based Noise Optimization
tldr_zh: 一步模型上以四个偏好 reward 之和对初始噪声做 50 步梯度上升（20–50 s），SD-Turbo GenEval 0.49→0.62
tldr_en: Gradient-ascent on initial noise of one-step T2I models with a sum of four preference rewards; 50 steps, 20-50 s, GenEval 0.49 to 0.62 for SD-Turbo.
key_numbers: GenEval mean: SD-Turbo 0.49 -> 0.62, SDXL-Turbo 0.54 -> 0.65, HyperSDXL 0.56 -> 0.65, FLUX-schnell 0.64 -> 0.72 (Table 3)
User study: SD-Turbo+ReNO beats SDXL 50-step 62.9%; HyperSDXL+ReNO beats SD3 54.6% (Fig. 4)
Cost: SD-Turbo 0.4 s/iter, 20 s total, 15 GB; HyperSDXL 1.0 s/iter, 50 s, 39 GB (Table 6)
vs DOODL: 100x faster, 75% less VRAM, attribute-binding gains +21.7/+28.9/+21.0 (Table 5)
Diversity (author-defined pairwise LPIPS/DINO similarity, lower = more diverse): SD-Turbo 0.382/0.770 -> +ReNO 0.246/0.712 (Table 4)
Prompt-independent LAION aesthetic reward raises the score without visual gain, i.e. reward hacking (Appendix E.5.3)
Hyperparameters: lambda_reg = 0.01 chi_d norm regularizer, lr 5, momentum 0.9, grad clip 0.1, 50 steps (Alg. 1, Appendix E.2)
